new_possibilities: The station table (station | what you see | what the feeler does): one grid that lets a student check their own run against the lesson in a glance. The original spreads it over three sentences.

“The mesh decides what is seen. The shape decides what is touched. Nothing forces them to agree.” A sharper statement of the lesson's hinge than the original's, worth keeping beside “We have chosen whether…”.

“Here, finally, the position from 1.2 gets used”: ties the unused-variable warning to its resolution. The warning goes away once something reads point_position. The original leaves that link implicit.

A one-line gloss of `:=`, and of why the script sets height to twice the radius: the original uses both and explains neither. The compression made the gaps visible by listing `:=` as code and showing the height line bare.
The museum consequence made bodily (“stopped by air”, sinking into something that looked solid). It gives the shortcut a place in the system it has to enter, the visitor's walk.
The feeler named as an instrument whose job is to tell touchable from untouchable. This states its epistemic role, which the original gives only as “borrowed equipment”.

“Keep the mismatch on purpose”, wrong as a step but alive as an invitation: after the restore, a closing line could offer a deliberate seen/touched mismatch as design material (the ghost wall, the invisible barrier). That fits QFEP's interest in surfaces that lie about their boundaries.

The Needs / Gives / Supplied contract read out as a student-facing line per section. The reader found the hidden comments useful but meta; shown on purpose, they make Palle's type-safety legible to a human reader too.

The stuck list as a research instrument: each stuck point names a referent the notation used before introducing it (feeler, label, museum, switch, corridor, held point, units). It is a ready checklist for L4.
lost_vectors: FORCE goes first. Only 1 of 13 force claims survives the compression intact (“Read, not paste”). The words that hold the lesson's limits are cut as redundant: “This is the whole script”, “Change only that line”, “only because the script makes it twice the radius”, “the contact test works without that overlay”, “Building the switch and its lighting rig is outside this lesson”, “without adding another required exercise”. The reader recovers some as marked guesses, but a scope guessed back is weaker than a scope stated.

THE RESTORES ARE THE LESSON'S STATE MACHINE, and all five were cut (“Restore 1.12”, “Restore the radius to 0.14”, “Restore sphere_shape.radius = radius”, “Return both to the matching 0.14”, and the first “Restore the height”). In type-safe terms they are each experiment's postcondition, the thing that makes the next section's “needs” true. Without them the unfolded runs the 0.35 experiment against a mesh of 0.3 carried over from another file, and offers to “keep the mismatch on purpose”. A connective with no content of its own carried the most hidden load.

DIRECTION AT THE END bends. Opening directions survive (aim, ready moment, nothing to surface to boundary), but all four forward-pointing ones are distorted. “The large sphere at the end of the museum corridor asks us to return to those choices… Knowing its construction gives us another way to change the encounter” becomes “yours to rebuild”: an encounter re-seen through knowledge turns into a construction task. “begins with a supplied point we can hold, then reads its movement. It will prepare two positions for the line” becomes “held point → two positions → line”, and then “draw a line between them”. The arrow cannot tell “prepare for” from “make”.

THE DEFERRAL turned around. “For now, this is the supplied position at our station. Point Coordinates will make its three components the subject of a lesson.” The original deliberately withholds coordinates. With that sentence cut, the reader filled the gap at once with x, y, z and “middle = height”, the very thing the curriculum postpones. Compression removed a restraint, and the unfolding read the silence as permission.

THE SHORTCUT'S LINK TO ITS SYSTEM. “Its movement is borrowed equipment, like the camera” and “It belongs to the supplied test, not to the position we have just defined” bind the feeler to the scaffold and cut it off from point_position. L3 keeps only a glossary entry, so the reader explained the first feeler's crossing by the missing body: true, and not the original's point (quiz 3). Likewise “The portable study keeps its supplied light” links the museum switch to the study; it is gone, and the unfolded nearly merges sun with the study's light.

THE STAND-IN, INVERTED. “In the museum, it is your movement that meets this difference. The fixed-camera study supplies another moving body so we can test the same relation.” Here the feeler stands in for the visitor because the camera is fixed. L3's “Museum: your movement is the feeler” makes the visitor stand in for the feeler, and drops the fixed camera that explains why a feeler exists at all.

≠ MAKES PROCEDURES INTO IDENTITIES. “A position and the object placed there are different things” becomes “Position ≠ body”. “Remove the light, keep the body” (an action with a result) becomes “Light ≠ body”. “We have chosen whether the surface we see and the boundary we encounter coincide” (a choice arrived at by doing) becomes “Seen ≠ touched: you choose” (a rule given in advance). The perfect tense of experience becomes the present tense of definition, and the glossary's “body = placed node” then collides with the original's “physics body”.

THE CODE CUT DROPPED A CARRYING LINE. L3's header promises “code cut to the lines that carry the idea”, but it cut `sphere.radius = radius`, the one line that, beside `sphere_shape.radius = radius`, makes surface and boundary share a radius (C82). The reader rebuilt it from Godot knowledge. A reader without that knowledge could not have.

THE ONE NAME OVER THREE BODIES. Each station has its own “Point one” label, and the corridor sphere “still says ‘Point one’”. The same name over nothing, a surface, a solid and a large sphere is the lesson's quiet figure: one point, many bodies. L3 kept the corridor's label and dropped the stations', and the unfolded guessed that each label names its own station.
“HIDES”. “We can change how much the sphere hides without changing what can pass through it.” Occlusion as an amount you control flattens into a binary of seen against touched.

THE SENSORY CHECKS. Small pink feelers moving left to right, the repeating sweep, a white sphere that “stays small”, long shadows against a dim fill, a wall switch, a large sphere. These are how a student checks the running scene against the text. Their absence produced the longest stuck point (what the feeler looks like and where it goes).
readability: Hard for this student: 0.75 on the quiz by the key, but 23 stuck points, most about referents the notation names without introducing them (feeler, label, museum, switch, corridor, held point) and about syntax (›, ·, →, ≠, +) that has to be decoded before the lesson can be read. The code read easily. The lesson's state (which number, which file, what to restore) could not be followed, and both of the reader's firm errors (mesh at 0.3, keep the mismatch) come from that. The unfolding needed 2.25 times the original's words to get back what it could.
